content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "What event or condition triggers the scheduling of a vendor meeting — is it a recurring calendar event, a specific equipment issue, a contract milestone, or something else?", "answer": "It usually comes up when there is some kind of need or situation that makes a meeting seem worthwhile. Nothing too formal triggers it."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "Which roles from your organization are expected to attend the vendor meeting, and who has the authority to approve or commit to improvement actions discussed?", "answer": "Generally the relevant people show up, and someone with enough authority tends to be involved when decisions need to be made."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "How is the meeting discussion captured — for example, are written notes taken during the meeting, is the session recorded, or is the summary produced from memory afterward?", "answer": "Someone usually keeps track of what is said in some way, and a summary gets put together afterward by whoever is responsible."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "At what point in the process are action items formally identified and assigned to owners — during the meeting itself, or during a separate post-meeting review step?", "answer": "It tends to happen at some point after the discussion, when people figure out who should handle what."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "What tool or method is currently used to track action item progress after the meeting, and how are reminders or escalations handled when a deadline is approaching or missed?", "answer": "There is usually some way of keeping an eye on things, and reminders get sent out when something seems overdue."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "What does a successfully completed process look like — what specific condition or output signals that this workflow instance is finished?", "answer": "It is more or less done when everything seems to be wrapped up and the relevant people feel the follow-up is handled."}]}
